notes: The sheet’s own word timing is used now. A timed sheet can stamp each word, and that was being stripped out of the line with the line stamps — every word after it was paced by a guess. The highlight lands on the stamp, and a word between two stamps is placed by its own syllables.

The recording’s measurement finally applies. The inline stamps were being counted as words, so the measured word count never matched the words on screen and the line fell back to the guess. Counting only the words that are drawn is what lets the voice time the words.

No word gets skipped. The light now moves to the last word the playhead has reached, instead of looking for a window to be inside — a fast pair of words, or a line whose words were bunched at its end, used to be stepped over entirely.
A line never sits dark waiting for its first word. If the singing starts a beat after the line’s stamp, the first word is lit for that stretch.
The light glides from one word to the next now instead of snapping. The sheet’s text, the line highlight, the scroll, the sync nudge and letter mode are unchanged.
